cfb.off_ppa.label: Opponent-adjusted offensive PPA/EPA and success rate
cfb.off_ppa.mechanism: Predicted points added per play measures offensive efficiency in expected-points units, and adjusting for defenses faced isolates how much scoring an offense produces per snap; it is the main driver of points per drive and margin.
cfb.off_ppa.rationale: College schedules are wildly unbalanced (FCS/G5 cupcakes versus P4), so raw per-play averages are heavily contaminated by opponent quality; adjustment needs a connected-schedule model, and early-season samples (12 games) require a preseason prior and garbage-time filtering.
cfb.off_ppa.measurement: From plays: PPA/EPA per play on non-garbage-time snaps (filter by score margin by quarter), split rush/pass; ridge-adjust for opponents (offense, defense, home) with recency weights; blend with a preseason prior from last year plus returning production weighted by 1/(1+n_games/k); report separately for the current QB.

cfb.def_ppa.label: Opponent-adjusted defensive PPA/EPA and success rate
cfb.def_ppa.mechanism: Defensive PPA allowed, adjusted for opposing offenses, measures how many expected points a defense prevents per snap and sets the baseline for opponent output.
cfb.def_ppa.rationale: Defense is less stable than offense across seasons in college because of turnover from portal and graduation; early-season ratings must lean on returning-production priors and individual unit (front seven versus secondary) changes.
cfb.def_ppa.measurement: Same ridge framework on defensive effect, splitting rush/pass, filtering garbage time; shrink toward prior from returning defensive production and recruiting talent; weight recent games; adjust for current injuries of defensive starters.

cfb.sp_plus.label: SP+/FPI-style composite ratings
cfb.sp_plus.mechanism: Published tempo- and opponent-adjusted composite ratings combine efficiency, explosiveness, finishing drives and turnover luck into a strength measure that captures much of team quality.
cfb.sp_plus.rationale: Composite ratings are strong priors and a benchmark for any home-built model; subtle points: their preseason versions rely on returning production and recruiting, and in-season values embed the same noise, so they are not independent from the underlying PPA inputs.
cfb.sp_plus.measurement: Pull SP+, FPI, SRS and Elo ratings by week and team; keep the version as of decision time (no revisions); compute rating difference with home adjustment and convert to margin via historical mapping; compare with market-implied margin to see residual.

cfb.talent.label: Recruiting talent composite and portal gains/losses
cfb.talent.mechanism: Roster talent (recruiting composite plus transfers) sets the long-run ceiling of a team and is the main preseason driver of strength, especially for depth and line play.
cfb.talent.rationale: Talent composites predict strength better than past win-loss at preseason and matter more at the extremes (blue-bloods versus small programs); they are slow-moving, so in-season play should dominate; the portal makes talent volatile year to year, so use the post-portal roster.
cfb.talent.measurement: CFBD team talent composite and recruiting classes (247 composite), net portal rating gains/losses by position group, weighted by position value; regression of margin vs talent difference after controlling for efficiency; shrink as games accumulate.

cfb.market_ratings.label: Market-implied team strength history
cfb.market_ratings.mechanism: Spreads and moneylines across the season encode sharp information on injuries, QB status and matchups; implied ratings are the strongest prior on team quality.
cfb.market_ratings.rationale: The market is typically well calibrated on spread; the model value is mostly incremental (lineup news, weather, totals) or on props and periods; a rating derived from lines must be tied to the lineup assumed by the line.
cfb.market_ratings.measurement: Invert closing spreads and totals into team ratings via a ridge/Bradley-Terry fit with home edge by season; keep time-varying ratings and the opener-to-close move; cross-check with SP+ and Elo.

cfb.cross_conf_calibration.label: Cross-conference calibration and schedule connectivity
cfb.cross_conf_calibration.mechanism: FBS teams play few cross-conference games, so ratings of different conferences are connected by a thin web of results; mis-calibrated conference strength distorts every opponent-adjusted stat.
cfb.cross_conf_calibration.rationale: A team with a great adjusted PPA inside a weak conference may be overrated relative to P4 opponents; the market corrects this with priors; calibration requires explicit conference effects estimated from non-conference games and shrinkage.
cfb.cross_conf_calibration.measurement: Add conference random effects to the ridge model (offense and defense separately), estimate from non-conference games and bowls with shrinkage; include FCS opponent indicator; check connectivity and use priors from past-year conference strength.

cfb.success_explosiveness.label: Success rate and explosiveness (IsoPPP) profile
cfb.success_explosiveness.mechanism: Efficiency (success rate) and explosiveness (IsoPPP) describe how an offense scores: consistent chain-moving versus big plays; the combination determines drive length, variance and totals.
cfb.success_explosiveness.rationale: Teams reliant on explosive plays have high variance and are less stable game to game; success-rate teams sustain drives and burn clock; this affects totals, team totals and the first-half/quarter distribution.
cfb.success_explosiveness.measurement: Opponent-adjusted success rate by down and distance and IsoPPP (average PPA on successful plays) for offense and defense; compute explosive-dependence index = z(IsoPPP) - z(success rate); shrink and weight recent games.

cfb.rush_efficiency.label: Rush efficiency: line yards, opportunity rate, stuff rate
cfb.rush_efficiency.mechanism: Rushing success relies on offensive-line production (line yards, opportunity rate), scheme and back-level creation; defenses differ in stuff rate and front quality.
cfb.rush_efficiency.rationale: Rushing yards, team totals and clock usage depend on run efficiency and volume; individual RB stats confuse OL with RB skill; need opponent adjustment given weak schedules.
cfb.rush_efficiency.measurement: From advanced stats: line yards per carry, opportunity rate, stuff rate, power success rate, highlight yards; opponent-adjust vs defense line yards allowed; shrink.

cfb.pass_efficiency.label: Pass efficiency: PPA/dropback, yards per attempt, sack rate
cfb.pass_efficiency.mechanism: Passing efficiency, QB quality and receiver/protection combination drive explosive scoring and variance in college, where pass rates vary from run-first to air-raid styles.
cfb.pass_efficiency.rationale: Passing yardage and TD props require adjusted pass efficiency vs opposing secondaries and rush; heavy variance between games; QB changes (transfers) shift it sharply.
cfb.pass_efficiency.measurement: PPA per dropback, adjusted yards per attempt, completion % over expected where charting exists, sack and INT rates; opponent adjust; blend with QB career prior and recency.

cfb.havoc.label: Havoc rate (TFL, forced fumbles, pass breakups) created and allowed
cfb.havoc.mechanism: Havoc plays disrupt drives, create turnovers and negative plays and are a persistent defensive trait while havoc allowed marks offensive instability.
cfb.havoc.rationale: Havoc is more stable than turnovers and predicts defensive success; offenses with high havoc allowed face low success and drive failure, affecting totals, and unstable red-zone outcomes.
cfb.havoc.measurement: Havoc rate = (TFL + forced fumbles + PBU + INT)/plays for defense, and allowed for offense; opponent-adjusted; compare to turnover luck to separate process from outcome.

cfb.pass_rush.label: Pass-rush and sack/pressure rates for and against
cfb.pass_rush.mechanism: Pass rush versus pass protection sets sacks, pressure-induced incompletions and turnover chances, which heavily influence passing props, drive stalls and scoring.
cfb.pass_rush.rationale: College lines vary widely in quality; a dominant rush against a poor OL generates a disproportionate share of negative plays and punts; sack rates are noisy but pressure/havoc proxies and line talent help.
cfb.pass_rush.measurement: Sack rate and adjusted sack rate for offense allowed and defense generated (standard/passing downs), opponent-adjusted; line talent composites and returning starters; QB mobility and time-to-throw proxies (screen share).

cfb.ol.label: Offensive and defensive line quality and continuity
cfb.ol.mechanism: Line quality (returning starters, snaps together, injuries) determines run blocking and pass protection, which affects every offensive efficiency stat.
cfb.ol.rationale: Line injuries are less publicized in college and the official injury reporting is poor; continuity measured by returning starts is a proxy; effects are larger in the trenches than skill positions for team efficiency.
cfb.ol.measurement: Returning offensive-line starts and snaps from rosters and prior-year play logs; depth chart changes; adjusted line yards and sack rates; weight by position (tackles more for pass pro); flag changes.
free_sources: ESPN public JSON (site.api.espn.com college-football scoreboard / summary / rankings / injuries)

cfb.secondary_coverage.label: Secondary coverage and explosive pass defense
cfb.secondary_coverage.mechanism: Secondary quality (pass breakups, explosive passes allowed, coverage) limits opposing passing efficiency and yardage and determines who can exploit it.
cfb.secondary_coverage.rationale: Pass defense in college is unstable and highly dependent on a few corners and safeties; matchup against air-raid or deep-pass offenses is particularly sensitive.
cfb.secondary_coverage.measurement: Passing success rate allowed, explosive pass rate allowed, pass-defense PPA, PBU rate; opponent-adjust; adjust for key DB absence/portal departures.

cfb.run_defense.label: Run defense and front-seven quality
cfb.run_defense.mechanism: Front-seven strength sets rushing success allowed, stuff rate and scoring opportunities, and controls how heavy the offense leans on the pass.
cfb.run_defense.rationale: Run defense is more stable than pass defense in college because of line depth and talent; run-first offenses face the largest effect; box counts differ by scheme.
cfb.run_defense.measurement: Line yards allowed, stuff rate, rushing PPA allowed, opponent-adjusted; talent composite for defensive line/linebackers; adjust for injuries.

cfb.turnover_luck.label: Turnover margin luck and fumble recovery regression
cfb.turnover_luck.mechanism: Turnovers swing possessions; much of team turnover margin (especially fumble recoveries and INT conversion) is luck that regresses, creating mean reversion in scoring and ratings.
cfb.turnover_luck.rationale: Ratings and market priors that overweight recent turnover margin overrate lucky teams; SP+ explicitly adjusts, so using raw margin gives mistakes in totals and side markets, particularly in small samples.
cfb.turnover_luck.measurement: Expected turnovers = fumbles x 0.5 recovery rate + INT expectation from PBU and pass attempts; luck = actual minus expected; regress ~80-90% to zero; use process stats (havoc, PBU, sacks) as the persistent part.

cfb.roster_continuity.label: Returning production and offseason roster churn
cfb.roster_continuity.mechanism: The share of last year's production returning (and position weight) governs how much past performance carries into the new season, particularly at QB, OL and defensive front.
cfb.roster_continuity.rationale: With the portal and NIL, roster churn is far larger than in the NFL; returning production is a key preseason predictor of SP+ changes; for in-season markets, the first 3-4 games carry high uncertainty.
cfb.roster_continuity.measurement: CFBD returning production (usage-weighted) overall, offense, defense; adjust by incoming transfers' prior production and recruit classes; regress last-year rating with coefficient by returning share; decay prior as games accumulate.

cfb.transfer_roster.label: Transfers, roster churn and eligibility
cfb.transfer_roster.mechanism: Incoming and outgoing transfers change starters, depth and unit quality quickly, and eligibility rules determine who can play.
cfb.transfer_roster.rationale: Portal additions are often immediate starters; out-transfers can gut a position group; roster data is incomplete and eligibility (waivers, extra year) can change late.
cfb.transfer_roster.measurement: Portal entries with destination, prior-year production and star rating; compute net production added/lost by position group; verify eligibility status from official rosters and news; use as adjustment to unit ratings.

cfb.opt_out_departures.label: Opt-outs, mid-season redshirt decisions and departures
cfb.opt_out_departures.mechanism: Bowl/playoff opt-outs, four-game redshirt rule decisions and early draft entries remove players from late-season or postseason games.
cfb.opt_out_departures.rationale: Postseason lineups differ from regular-season ones, and players with NFL futures may sit; the information comes late through announcements and beat reports.
cfb.opt_out_departures.measurement: Track announced opt-outs and draft declarations with timestamp, estimate production share lost per player (usage), and update team and prop rating; base rates by draft prospect status and bowl type.

cfb.suspension_eligibility.label: Suspensions, targeting ejections and eligibility events
cfb.suspension_eligibility.mechanism: Disciplinary suspensions, first-half targeting suspensions and eligibility rulings remove players for specific games or halves.
cfb.suspension_eligibility.rationale: Targeting ejections carry into the next game for the first half; such events are public but irregular and not in standard feeds; the effect depends on player importance.
cfb.suspension_eligibility.measurement: Collect ejection/targeting events from play-by-play and official reports and map to next-game first-half unavailability; incorporate news-based suspensions with timestamp.

cfb.qb.label: Starting QB status and QB performance/regime
cfb.qb.mechanism: The starting QB is the largest single determinant of team offense in college; QB transfers, injuries and benchings cause large rating shifts.
cfb.qb.rationale: QB identity is often announced late (or not at all), and backups can be very different from starters; production by QB (not team) must drive projections, with priors for new QBs from transfer or recruiting profile.
cfb.qb.measurement: Per-QB PPA, completion %, sack and INT rates, rushing contribution; shrink small samples with prior from recruiting rating and previous team; map QB changes to team rating shifts; use mixture when status is uncertain.
free_sources: ESPN public JSON (site.api.espn.com college-football scoreboard / summary / rankings / injuries)

cfb.qb_status_pit.label: Confirmed QB/starter status with timestamped vintages
cfb.qb_status_pit.mechanism: Timestamped starter confirmation (depth chart, beat report, pregame warmup) sets whether the line and props assume the right QB.
cfb.qb_status_pit.rationale: No reliable official feed exists, so capture time matters: a QB known only at kickoff is not pregame-knowable for earlier-closing markets; sources are noisy and sometimes deliberately misleading.
cfb.qb_status_pit.measurement: Collect depth charts and beat reporter posts with timestamps; label confirmation vintage (Mon-Fri, game-day), compute probability the listed QB starts by source reliability and historical hit rates.
free_sources: ESPN public JSON (site.api.espn.com college-football scoreboard / summary / rankings / injuries)

cfb.injuries.label: Injury and availability news (no reliable official feed)
cfb.injuries.mechanism: Player availability changes team ratings and props, but college teams are not required to report injuries (only conference-level availability reports have started).
cfb.injuries.rationale: Information is sparse and unequal across conferences; late scratches are common; use of available-player reports where they exist (Big Ten/SEC/ACC/Big 12 policies) is partial and recent; absence must be inferred from usage drops and beat news.
cfb.injuries.measurement: Collect injury/availability reports where conferences publish, ESPN injuries, and beat-reporter posts with timestamps; track usage-based indicators (snaps drop); weight by player value; record vintage to avoid look-ahead.
free_sources: ESPN public JSON (site.api.espn.com college-football scoreboard / summary / rankings / injuries)

cfb.depth_chart.label: Depth chart / starters
cfb.depth_chart.mechanism: Depth charts list starters and ordering at each position and show role changes entering the game.
cfb.depth_chart.rationale: Depth charts in college are team-published, strategic and sometimes unreliable (OR designations); they lag changes but combine with usage and snap data to infer roles.
cfb.depth_chart.measurement: Weekly depth-chart snapshots with changes since last week; reconcile with play-by-play usage; flag OR positions and first-time starters; use as feature for player-stat markets.
free_sources: ESPN public JSON (site.api.espn.com college-football scoreboard / summary / rankings / injuries)

cfb.skill_avail.label: WR/TE/RB availability and replacement quality
cfb.skill_avail.mechanism: Skill-player availability redistributes targets and carries and lowers efficiency when replaced by lower-quality players.
cfb.skill_avail.rationale: In college, depth drops sharply behind starters, so absence of a top receiver or back has larger efficiency effects than in the NFL; availability news is sparse.
cfb.skill_avail.measurement: Vacated target/carry share and PPA of absent players; allocate to teammates with historical splits shrunk by sample; adjust efficiency by replacement quality (recruiting rating).
free_sources: ESPN public JSON (site.api.espn.com college-football scoreboard / summary / rankings / injuries)

cfb.qb_rushing.label: QB rushing usage and mobility
cfb.qb_rushing.mechanism: Dual-threat QBs add designed runs and scrambles, rushing yards and TDs, and change defense (spy) and offense (RPO) dynamics, important in college.
cfb.qb_rushing.rationale: QB rushing props and anytime TD depend on scheme; sack yardage counts against rushing in college stats (important for settlement); mobility reduces with injury.
cfb.qb_rushing.measurement: QB carries, designed run share, scramble rate, goal-line carries, yards before sack adjustments from plays; opponent adjust; shrink; check how stats source counts sacks.

cfb.player_usage.label: Player target, carry and snap share
cfb.player_usage.mechanism: Target and carry shares determine volume of player props; college roles are more volatile due to depth rotation and blowouts.
cfb.player_usage.rationale: Usage is persistent for starters but depends on game script; rotation and garbage-time substitutions in blowouts decrease volume for starters; depth charts help.
cfb.player_usage.measurement: Rolling target/carry share, red-zone share, snap share by game state from play logs; project volume = team plays x share; adjust for script/blowout probability and injuries.

cfb.td_rates.label: Anytime and first-TD scoring rates by role
cfb.td_rates.mechanism: Player TD probability derives from team expected TDs and the player's red-zone/goal-line share, including QB rushing scores.
cfb.td_rates.rationale: College teams have more variance in offense and sharper role specialization (goal-line backs, mobile QBs); small samples require shrinkage and regression of TD luck.
cfb.td_rates.measurement: Team expected TDs from total/spread; shares from red-zone carries/targets, QB sneak rate, goal-line role; calibrate with shrinkage; first-TD multiplies by P(team scores first).

cfb.dvp.label: Defense versus position and receiver/back matchup
cfb.dvp.mechanism: How a defense allows yards and TDs to RBs, WRs and TEs (opponent-adjusted) indicates which player types benefit in a matchup.
cfb.dvp.rationale: Raw defense-vs-position reflects opponents faced; the useful form is adjusted per-target efficiency and share; heavily shrunk in college because of weak schedule connectivity.
cfb.dvp.measurement: Allowed yards and PPA per target/carry by position adjusted for opponents (ridge), schedule connectivity shrinkage; combine with player share to forecast.

cfb.offense_style.label: Offensive style clash (option, air raid, RPO, tempo) and defensive preparation
cfb.offense_style.mechanism: Unconventional schemes (triple option, heavy RPO, air raid) produce atypical pace, run/pass splits and variance, and opponents' preparation and scheme fit alter results.
cfb.offense_style.rationale: Style mismatch explains outsized rushing totals (service academies) and unusual totals; defenses face unfamiliar schemes once per year, so adjusted ratings may understate or overstate effect; teams with long bye weeks prepare better.
cfb.offense_style.measurement: Classify teams by scheme using pass rate, option share, tempo and formation; estimate style-specific residuals of spread/total; adjust opponent defenses for familiarity (bye, prior exposure); shrink.

cfb.coaching.label: Coaching changes, scheme and tempo tendencies
cfb.coaching.mechanism: Head coach and coordinator regimes determine tempo, run/pass mix, 4th-down aggression and in-game management, changing volume and variance.
cfb.coaching.rationale: Coaching changes cause large preseason rating changes and early-season volatility; coaching tenure and experience influence close-game performance and handling of blowouts.
cfb.coaching.measurement: Coach/coordinator history for pace, pass rate, 4th-down go rate (fourth-down model), 2-pt rate, blowout behavior; regime-break dates; new-coach prior from previous stops; shrink.

cfb.pace.label: Plays per game, tempo and no-huddle rate
cfb.pace.mechanism: Plays per game and seconds per play set the number of possessions and counting stats; college tempo ranges far wider than NFL.
cfb.pace.rationale: Pace is stable and strongly regime-based; matchup pace is a function of both offenses and clock rules; run-heavy teams lower total plays; the effect on totals is large given the variance in tempo.
cfb.pace.measurement: Seconds per play on neutral situations, plays per game, no-huddle rate (non-garbage); combine pace of both teams (e.g., weighted average with opponent-adjusted tempo), and clock rules by season; recency-weight.

cfb.drives.label: Drives per game, explosiveness and finishing drives
cfb.drives.mechanism: Drive count and points per scoring opportunity set total scoring, and are driven by pace, turnover rate, quick scores and clock management.
cfb.drives.rationale: Possession-level modelling accounts for the fact that explosive offenses may play few plays but many drives; finishing (red-zone, 4th down) is a partly persistent skill.
cfb.drives.measurement: Drives per game, plays per drive, available yards, points per scoring opportunity, drive-level success; opponent adjusted; forecast drives = f(pace both teams, turnover rates, expected script).

cfb.pass_rate.label: Pass rate and script behaviour
cfb.pass_rate.mechanism: Pass rate in neutral situations and its response to score determines pass attempts, passing yards and time of possession.
cfb.pass_rate.rationale: College run/pass splits vary strongly by team style; spread-based game script drives volume; late-game leader run rate affects clock and total.
cfb.pass_rate.measurement: Neutral-situation pass rate (non-garbage), pass rate over expected by down/distance/score; response slope to score difference; forecast attempts under the spread-implied script distribution.

cfb.clock_rules.label: Clock rules regime by season (first-down clock stops, play clock)
cfb.clock_rules.mechanism: College clock rules (whether the clock stops after first downs, stoppages after incompletions, play-clock details) change plays per game and total scoring across seasons.
cfb.clock_rules.rationale: Rule changes shift pace and totals; model training must account for regime breaks; recent rule changes reduce plays, requiring older seasons to be adjusted.
cfb.clock_rules.measurement: Indicator variables for rule regime by season, with regime-specific mean plays and scoring; re-estimate pace baseline after each rule change; adjust for tempo teams that benefit most.
free_sources: CollegeFootballData API (free key) /plays (plays per game by season)

cfb.field_pos.label: Field position, special teams and kicking
cfb.field_pos.mechanism: Starting field position and special teams (returns, punts, kickoffs, field goals) add expected points per drive and are highly variable in college.
cfb.field_pos.rationale: Special-teams quality is highly variable by program (kicker/punter talent), and kickoff/touchback rules affect starting spots; effect is persistent but small versus offense, and larger in low-scoring games.
cfb.field_pos.measurement: Average starting field position for each side, net punting, return EPA, FG%/range; opponent-adjusted; shrink; consider rule regime changes (fair catch on kickoff).

cfb.kicker.label: Kicker accuracy by distance, effective range, FG attempt rate
cfb.kicker.mechanism: Kicker make probability by distance and the coach's FG-attempt policy determine how many stalled drives yield 3 points and total-line key-number structure.
cfb.kicker.rationale: College kickers have wide quality variance and few attempts; shrinkage is crucial; wind, altitude and dome conditions matter; coach aggressiveness on 4th down changes FG attempts.
cfb.kicker.measurement: Make probability by distance with random kicker effect and weather covariates; FG attempt rate by field position and score; kickoff touchback rates; shrink small samples.

cfb.redzone.label: Red-zone efficiency and FG versus TD
cfb.redzone.mechanism: Red-zone TD rate converts yards into points; skill and personnel (goal-line QB runs) contribute but variance is large.
cfb.redzone.rationale: In small college samples red-zone rates regress strongly; teams with unusual goal-line schemes (QB sneak, power run) are partly persistent; matters for totals and team totals.
cfb.redzone.measurement: Red-zone TD%, points per trip, goal-to-go success; shrink toward league mean and expected rate from yardage and field position; opponent adjust; recency weighting.

cfb.script.label: Opening script, early-game scripting and blowout/garbage-time behaviour
cfb.script.mechanism: Early scripted plays, pass/run response to score, and starters' removal in blowouts shape quarter/half scoring and player stat volume.
cfb.script.rationale: The spread-implied script drives pace and run/pass splits; heavy favorites change style in the second half; garbage time changes player usage and yardage.
cfb.script.measurement: Pace and pass rate as functions of score differential and time; opening-drive pass rate; blowout multiplier for second-half pace; integrate over distribution of states from spread/total.

cfb.blowout_management.label: Blowout management and starter removal
cfb.blowout_management.mechanism: Large favorites pull starters, run clock and play backups once ahead, reducing the favorite's points and shifting garbage-time points to the underdog.
cfb.blowout_management.rationale: College mismatches (FCS or large P4-vs-G5 spreads) are common; coach-specific lead behavior decides how many points the favorite scores in the second half, directly affecting team totals, totals, and the cover probability for big spreads.
cfb.blowout_management.measurement: For each coach/team: second-half pace, pass rate and points when leading by 21+, share of starters' snaps in Q4; estimate probability of 21+ lead from spread and apply behavior; shrink.

cfb.opening_poss.label: Opening possession (coin toss/deferral) and first-quarter pace
cfb.opening_poss.mechanism: Who receives first and the deferral habits shift first-quarter scoring and the halftime possession order, influencing first-half and first-quarter markets.
cfb.opening_poss.rationale: Coin toss is random; teams' deferral tendency is coach-specific; knowledge is revealed only at the toss, so pregame markets need a mixture.
cfb.opening_poss.measurement: Team and coach defer rate; first-quarter scoring by possession order; adjust the first-quarter and first-half distribution with a 50/50 mixture.

cfb.first_drive.label: Opening-drive tendencies and outcomes
cfb.first_drive.mechanism: Scripted first drives show team-specific tempo, run/pass mix and scoring rates that feed first-quarter and first-TD markets.
cfb.first_drive.rationale: The first drives are pre-scripted and efficient for some teams but the sample per team is small (12-14 games), requiring pooling.
cfb.first_drive.measurement: Share of first drives ending in TD/FG/punt/turnover, plays and tempo; opponent adjust; shrink with prior of ~20 drives.

cfb.q_scoring.label: Historical scoring by quarter and half, opponent-adjusted
cfb.q_scoring.mechanism: Scoring by period reveals first-half vs second-half profile, slow starters, blowout fade and end-of-half scoring, needed for quarter and half markets.
cfb.q_scoring.rationale: Period markets require period-specific rates; college blowouts distort Q3-Q4 more than in the NFL; adjusted rates avoid conflating weak opponents.
cfb.q_scoring.measurement: Per team points and plays by quarter and half (opponent adjusted); period share of game scoring; combine with the game total; shrink.

cfb.half_split.label: First/second-half scoring split and adjustments
cfb.half_split.mechanism: Teams adjust at halftime and starters' usage differs when leading; consistent patterns in first-half versus second-half scoring exist for coaches and styles.
cfb.half_split.rationale: Halftime-adjustment skill is noisy, but structural effects such as ball-control teams and blowout behavior persist; second-half totals are more sensitive to the script.
cfb.half_split.measurement: Ratio of first-half to full-game points for team and opponents, conditional on spread bins; hierarchical shrinkage; link to coaching and script.

cfb.score_resid.label: Score residual distribution around lines (key numbers)
cfb.score_resid.mechanism: Final margins and totals relative to lines are fat-tailed in college (blowouts, FCS mismatches) and cluster at key numbers (3, 7, 10, 14).
cfb.score_resid.rationale: Normal approximations misprice tails and push-adjacent lines; college SD of margin versus spread is larger than NFL and increases with spread size.
cfb.score_resid.measurement: Empirical distribution of margin - closing spread and total - closing total by spread bucket and conference tier, with key-number mass; scale variance with total and spread size.

cfb.ot_model.label: Overtime rules and tie/OT model
cfb.ot_model.mechanism: College overtime alternates possessions from the opponent's 25-yard line with no ties, and later overtimes require 2-point attempts, so overtime outcomes and scoring differ from the NFL.
cfb.ot_model.rationale: Regulation tie probability and OT length determine overtime markets, and moneyline/spread wording determines whether OT points count; the effective rules changed over years and must match the sample period.
cfb.ot_model.measurement: P(tied after 60 minutes) from margin distribution with key-number mass; OT possession outcomes (score probability from the 25), number of OT periods distribution (2-point rule from later periods); mapping to settlement wording.

cfb.corr.label: Within-game correlation across stats, periods and teams
cfb.corr.mechanism: Scores, periods and player stats are correlated through script, pace and mismatch; independence assumptions misprice joint events.
cfb.corr.rationale: Quarter/half legs, team totals and player stats share the same latent drives; mismatch games have particular correlation structure (favorite and total).
cfb.corr.measurement: Estimate correlations of residuals (team scores, period totals, player stats) from game-level data; model through simulation of drives or copulas; calibrate.

cfb.team_total_split.label: Team-points split from game total and spread
cfb.team_total_split.mechanism: Team totals must satisfy the game total and spread implied means; deviations indicate mispricing or lineup differences.
cfb.team_total_split.rationale: Team-total markets often lag lineup news; the split also depends on pace asymmetry and blowout behavior.
cfb.team_total_split.measurement: Compute implied means from spread and total; adjust for team-specific variance and blowout behavior; compare team-total quotes with implied split.

cfb.player_stat_variance.label: Player-stat distribution shape and volatility
cfb.player_stat_variance.mechanism: The dispersion of player stats around expectation (usage volatility, garbage time, injuries) determines rung probabilities.
cfb.player_stat_variance.rationale: College player stats are more volatile than the NFL because of rotation, blowouts and heavy matchup variance; ladders need mixtures.
cfb.player_stat_variance.measurement: Fit game-level distributions (negative binomial/zero-inflated) with dispersion by role; include blowout and exit mixture components; compute exceedance probabilities.

cfb.weather_pit.label: Kickoff-hour weather forecast vintages
cfb.weather_pit.mechanism: Wind, rain and cold reduce passing and kicking performance and shift run rates, with stronger effects in open college stadiums.
cfb.weather_pit.rationale: Forecast vintages matter; effects are nonlinear; many college stadiums are open-air; extreme weather leads to delays or cancellations (lifecycle).
cfb.weather_pit.measurement: Store forecasts at fixed lead times by stadium coordinates (wind, gusts, precipitation, temperature); ignore domes; compute effect on totals, pass rate and FG success.

cfb.venue.label: Venue, altitude, home-field and crowd effect
cfb.venue.mechanism: Home-field advantage in college is large and variable (crowd, travel, altitude) and neutral-site games remove it.
cfb.venue.rationale: College HFA differs by program and stadium; neutral-site and bowl games should be modeled with zero or small HFA; altitude or noise affects tempo and false starts.
cfb.venue.measurement: Venue table (capacity, altitude, surface, roof), team-specific HFA estimated with shrinkage; neutral-site indicator; crowd/attendance signal.

cfb.rest_travel.label: Rest, travel, bye, short week and lookahead/rivalry
cfb.rest_travel.mechanism: Rest days, travel distance and schedule position (bye, short week, lookahead and letdown spots) influence performance and preparation.
cfb.rest_travel.rationale: College schedules have weekly rhythm with occasional short weeks and byes; effects are modest but can be notable for emotional spots; the market partly prices them.
cfb.rest_travel.measurement: Days of rest, bye previous week, travel distance/time zone, kickoff time, rivalry and next-opponent importance flags; regress margin residuals on these with shrinkage.

cfb.motivation.label: Bowl/CFP eligibility, rivalry and standings stakes
cfb.motivation.mechanism: Stakes such as bowl eligibility, conference title, playoff berth, rivalry or coach transitions alter effort and personnel decisions.
cfb.motivation.rationale: Motivation is a notable factor in late-season and bowl games: opt-outs, transfers and coaching changes interact; hard to quantify, so use structured flags.
cfb.motivation.measurement: Flags for bowl eligibility at stake, CFP implications (change in playoff probability), rivalry, eliminated/clinched; from standings simulation compute marginal game importance.

cfb.officials.label: Officiating crew penalty tendencies
cfb.officials.mechanism: Crews vary in flag rates (holding, pass interference, targeting) that shift drive length, scoring and ejections.
cfb.officials.rationale: College crews are conference-specific, so effects are intertwined with conference style; data on crew assignments are not widely published.
cfb.officials.measurement: Crew-level penalties per game with team adjustment (random effects) when assignments are available; otherwise conference-level penalty tendencies.

cfb.standings.label: Conference standings, tiebreakers and CFP ranking model

cfb.standings.rationale: Selection involves committee judgement and format changes (12-team playoff), so simulations must encode rules and uncertain committee behaviour.
cfb.standings.measurement: Monte Carlo of remaining games with ratings uncertainty; conference tiebreakers; playoff selection model (rank-based with historical committee behavior).

cfb.polls.label: Poll and ranking dynamics and committee behaviour
cfb.polls.mechanism: Rankings influence perceived strength, committee decisions and market-based futures; their movements follow predictable patterns after wins and losses.
cfb.polls.rationale: Committee rankings anchor playoff odds; movement depends on game results and quality; useful for markets resolved by rankings.
cfb.polls.measurement: Weekly rankings history (AP, coaches, CFP); model transition probabilities conditional on result, margin and opponent rank.

cfb.playoff_format.label: Playoff format and seeding rules in force
cfb.playoff_format.mechanism: The format (number of teams, automatic bids, seeding, byes, home-field) defines how strength translates into title and berth probabilities.
cfb.playoff_format.rationale: Rules changed recently; futures and make-playoff markets need the exact format and bracket; wrong rule set gives structurally wrong probabilities.
cfb.playoff_format.measurement: Document format by season (bids, seeding, tiebreakers, bracket paths, neutral/home sites); encode in simulation; check contract wording.

cfb.schedule_strength.label: Remaining and conference schedule strength
cfb.schedule_strength.mechanism: Remaining opponents and home/away distribution determine expected wins and playoff paths.
cfb.schedule_strength.rationale: College schedules are unbalanced across conferences; remaining schedule difficulty is a central input to futures and rankings.
cfb.schedule_strength.measurement: Sum of win probabilities over remaining games using current ratings with home/rest adjustments; correlation within conference; compare to market.

cfb.pythag_luck.label: Close-game record and Pythagorean luck
cfb.pythag_luck.mechanism: Records in one-score games and points-based expected wins deviate from true strength; lucky records regress.
cfb.pythag_luck.rationale: Season futures and rankings based on record overstate lucky teams; Pythagorean/advanced-stat wins are better predictors.
cfb.pythag_luck.measurement: Pythagorean wins and PPA-based expected wins; one-score game record vs expectation; regress most of the luck.

cfb.award_narrative.label: Award candidates (Heisman) production and narrative
cfb.award_narrative.mechanism: Awards like the Heisman follow production, team success, QB/position bias and narrative in an electorate that is known and timed.
cfb.award_narrative.rationale: Winners are mostly QBs on top-ranked teams; narrative changes weekly; ballots close before certain late games.
cfb.award_narrative.measurement: Candidate stats and team rank, historical winners model, odds path, ballot timeline; update weekly.

cfb.futures_coherence.label: Cross-market coherence for season-level futures
cfb.futures_coherence.mechanism: Conference, playoff, title and ranking markets are linked by sum-to-one and implication constraints.
cfb.futures_coherence.rationale: Violations identify stale quotes; linked markets share common uncertainty about team strength.
cfb.futures_coherence.measurement: Aggregate related contracts, compute sum of mids and monotonic constraints, compare with model.

cfb.in_game_exit_risk.label: In-game injury exit and starter removal risk
cfb.in_game_exit_risk.mechanism: Players exiting mid-game (injury, blowout rest) truncate counting stats and shift volume to backups.
cfb.in_game_exit_risk.rationale: In college, blowouts remove starters early and injuries are common; the risk is a hidden haircut to stat props.
cfb.in_game_exit_risk.measurement: Estimate probability of missing a chunk of snaps by role using historical snap-share distributions, blowout probability and injury status; apply as mixture.

m.quote_history.label: Kalshi bid/ask/last time series through close
m.quote_history.mechanism: The market's own price path aggregates information over time and is the benchmark any model must beat; movements around news and lineup release show how quickly information is absorbed.
m.quote_history.rationale: Closing price is a strong prior; the useful question is whether early prices lag information (injury news, weather forecasts, lineup release) or overreact; the time-to-close and vintage of each quote must be recorded so research is point-in-time. Last-trade can be stale in thin markets; mid of bid/ask is more informative.
m.quote_history.measurement: Store timestamped bid, ask, last and volume candlesticks for each contract; compute mid, spread, time since last trade, drift from open to close and price at fixed horizons (24h, 3h, 1h, 5m before start); use as prior/benchmark and for closing-line value computations.

m.orderbook_depth.label: Order-book depth and spread
m.orderbook_depth.mechanism: Depth and spread determine how much size can be executed at a price and the cost of crossing; thin books imply noisy mids and slippage.
m.orderbook_depth.rationale: Edge estimated from mid price is not realizable if the executable price is worse; depth also signals liquidity providers' confidence; wide spreads in props/ladder rungs mean much of the model edge is consumed.
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Snapshot orderbook levels (price, size) per contract; compute spread, depth at top 3 levels, expected fill price for a given size; track by time to start and rung; compare with model edge.

m.volume_oi.label: Volume and open interest
m.volume_oi.mechanism: Volume and open interest measure participation and price reliability; high-volume markets are better aggregated while low-volume ones can be stale or manipulated.
m.volume_oi.rationale: Information content of the price scales with volume; low-volume rungs may lag; volume spikes follow news and identify reaction windows.
m.volume_oi.measurement: Per-contract cumulative volume, open interest and volume velocity by time before start; use as reliability weight for price benchmarks and for execution feasibility.

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of threshold ladders
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: Threshold ladders (over 199.5, 249.5, 299.5 ...) must be monotone and jointly define an implied distribution; inconsistencies or a kinked implied density reveal stale or mispriced rungs.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Correlated rungs mean a model error propagates across rungs, so edges at adjacent thresholds are not independent bets; rung spacing and push rules (half-point lines avoid pushes) change settlement; implied mean/median from the ladder can be compared with model forecast.
m.ladder_structure.measurement: Fit a smooth CDF to rung prices (isotonic or parametric, e.g. negative binomial), check monotonicity, compute implied mean/SD/skew and implied mass between rungs; detect rungs deviating from fitted curve; treat adjacent rungs as one position in sizing.
free_sources: Kalshi public market API (markets, candlesticks, trades, orderbook)

m.settlement_truth.label: Settled result, settlement value and timestamp
m.settlement_truth.mechanism: The settlement value and time define ground truth for training and evaluation; discrepancies between source stats and settled outcomes expose rule or source risk.
m.settlement_truth.rationale: Labels must be the settled outcomes with exact definitions (regulation vs including overtime, official stats), not recomputed from convenient sources; timing of settlement affects capital.
m.settlement_truth.measurement: Pull settled results (result, settlement value, settlement time) for each market and reconcile with independent box-score source; track mismatch rate and delay between event end and settlement.

m.rules_text.label: Versioned rules and settlement wording (overtime, ties, postponement, void)
m.rules_text.mechanism: The rules text defines what counts: whether overtime is included, how pushes, ties, player DNP, postponements, and stat corrections are handled; the same football event can settle differently across contracts.
m.rules_text.rationale: Probability models must match the exact settlement clause; e.g. a regulation-only market has a tie mass while an including-OT market does not; void and DNP rules change whether a prop is a loss or a refund; rule text may change between versions.
m.rules_text.measurement: Collect rules_primary/secondary text per contract with version/timestamp; parse for OT inclusion, push/tie treatment, void conditions, data source and expiration; map to the model output definition and flag ambiguous clauses.
free_sources: Kalshi public market API (markets, candlesticks, trades, orderbook)

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook and exchange reference prices with timestamps
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sharp sportsbook and exchange prices are a high-information benchmark for game, props and futures; comparing Kalshi to them tests for staleness or inefficiency.
m.external_lines.rationale: Using the right reference matters: de-vig, line timing and book selection change the implied probability; closing lines at sharp books are best proxies for true probability, while opening lines are noisy.
m.external_lines.measurement: Collect timestamped lines for spread, total, moneyline, props and futures; remove vig by multiplicative/power method; compute cross-book consensus and its lead/lag versus Kalshi quotes.

m.fees.label: Fee schedule and maker/taker rules
m.fees.mechanism: Fees reduce realized edge and scale with price (larger near 50c), changing which markets and thresholds are tradable.
m.fees.rationale: A model edge of a few cents may vanish after fees and spread; fees and maker/taker rebates differ by time and market type, so the cost model must follow the schedule in force at trade time.
m.fees.measurement: Maintain fee schedule versions and compute fee per contract at each price; net edge = model probability - price - fees - slippage; include maker/taker difference.

m.lifecycle.label: Open/close/halt/postponement lifecycle events
m.lifecycle.mechanism: Market lifecycle (opening time, trading halts, close, early determination or postponement) controls when information can be used and when exposure ends.
m.lifecycle.rationale: A market that closes at kickoff versus one that remains open during play uses different information sets; postponed or suspended games trigger void/extension rules.
m.lifecycle.measurement: Track created/open/close/settle timestamps and status changes per ticker; compute time from open to start and close to start; flag delayed/postponed games; define decision time for point-in-time features.
free_sources: Kalshi public market API (markets, candlesticks, trades, orderbook)

m.strike_hit_rates.label: Historical realized frequency by strike and rung per family
m.strike_hit_rates.mechanism: Realized frequencies for each strike in a family (e.g. QB over 250.5) provide an empirical calibration baseline and expose systematic bias in how rungs are priced.
m.strike_hit_rates.rationale: Thresholds around round numbers and half-point lines can show systematic over/under pricing (favorite-longshot bias); empirical hit rates need sufficient sample and conditioning on season/regime.
m.strike_hit_rates.measurement: From settled contracts: hit rate by family, threshold relative to expected (or ladder percentile) and price bucket; compute calibration curve (price vs realized) with confidence intervals; compare across seasons.
free_sources: Kalshi public market API (markets, candlesticks, trades, orderbook)

m.trade_tape.label: Executed trades (price, size, taker side, time)
m.trade_tape.mechanism: The trade tape shows executed prices, sizes and aggressor side, revealing order flow, information arrival and realistic fill prices.
m.trade_tape.rationale: Mid quotes can be stale; trades show where liquidity actually transacted and whether flow is informed (one-sided aggressive buying before news); needed for realistic slippage and CLV.
m.trade_tape.measurement: Collect trades with timestamps, count, taker side; compute volume-weighted price, signed order flow imbalance before news, and execution slippage vs mid; use with candlesticks to measure price impact.
free_sources: Kalshi public market API (markets, candlesticks, trades, orderbook)

m.stat_source_mismatch.label: Official versus provider stat definition and source mismatch
m.stat_source_mismatch.mechanism: College statistics differ across sources (NCAA official, ESPN, school stat crews) and in definitions (sack yardage counted against rushing, bowl and conference game inclusion), so thresholds near a boundary can resolve differently.
m.stat_source_mismatch.rationale: Stat props resolve on a named source; if the model is trained on another source the label is wrong; corrections after the game and differences in treatment (kneel-downs, sacks) are sources of tail risk especially around round thresholds.
m.stat_source_mismatch.measurement: Compare player/team stats across at least two sources for completed games and record mismatch rates by stat; identify the contract source and lock time; flag ladders where realized values fall within typical mismatch tolerance.
free_sources: Kalshi public market API (markets, candlesticks, trades, orderbook)

cfb.season_sim_distribution.label: Season simulation distribution (CFP, conference title, win totals)
cfb.season_sim_distribution.mechanism: Season outcomes are order statistics of a simulated schedule with rating uncertainty, injury risk and committee rules.
cfb.season_sim_distribution.rationale: Point ratings answer who is better; futures markets ask for the probability of a rank or title, which needs the simulated distribution including tiebreakers, conference championship games and the committee's ranking behaviour. Subtle: correlated outcomes (two teams in one conference) matter for head-to-head and top-N markets.
cfb.season_sim_distribution.measurement: Monte Carlo of the remaining schedule using own power ratings with rating uncertainty (Bayesian updating after each game), conference tiebreaker rules and a committee-ranking model fitted to past rankings; report rank and title probabilities.

cfb.award_vote_distribution.label: Award vote-share distribution (Heisman and conference awards)
cfb.award_vote_distribution.mechanism: Awards are decided by voter shares driven by production, team success and narrative.
cfb.award_vote_distribution.rationale: Heisman-style markets need a probability distribution over candidates; quarterbacks on top-ranked teams dominate, and late-season games weigh more. Subtle: voting is regionally clustered and respects a candidate's bowl/CFP stage only in some years.
cfb.award_vote_distribution.measurement: Conditional-logit on historical winners and finalists with production percentile, team rank, prime-time exposure and position; calibrate by season.

cfb.poll_voter_behavior.label: AP poll and CFP committee ranking behaviour
cfb.poll_voter_behavior.mechanism: Poll rank and committee ranking move with results, opponent rank and narrative in patterned ways.
cfb.poll_voter_behavior.rationale: Rank markets (AP top-N, #1 any week, CFP seed) depend on how voters and the committee react to wins and losses: ranking inertia, penalty for losing as a favourite, bonus for ranked wins, and committee statements. Subtle: the AP poll and the CFP rankings follow different processes and calendars.
cfb.poll_voter_behavior.measurement: Historical week-over-week rank transitions conditional on result type, opponent rank and margin for the AP poll; committee ranking changes conditional on results and strength-of-record; fit ordered-response models.

cfb.offfield_base_rate.label: Reference-class base rates for coaching, conference and facility events
cfb.offfield_base_rate.mechanism: Coach exits, conference moves and facility milestones occur at historical frequencies tied to the calendar and team circumstances.
cfb.offfield_base_rate.rationale: These markets cannot be modelled from game data; the honest prior is the historical frequency of the event class by calendar window (coach exits by record and tenure, realignment announcements by cycle), updated by dated reporting.
cfb.offfield_base_rate.measurement: Count event classes per season and week-of-year from archives; condition on team record, tenure and buyout; shrink with an empirical-Bayes prior; record the announcement timestamp.

cfb.qb_replacement_value.label: Quarterback replacement value in points
cfb.qb_replacement_value.mechanism: Converts a confirmed or doubtful quarterback change into an expected-margin shift in points per game.
cfb.qb_replacement_value.rationale: Identity of the starter (cfb.qb_status_pit) is a vintage, not a number. A backup with 40 career dropbacks has a very wide EPA/play posterior, so the swap cost is both a mean shift and a variance increase; the market tends to over- or under-react depending on prior-year snaps.
cfb.qb_replacement_value.measurement: For each team-season, starter value = EPA per dropback (incl. designed rushes) over the last 2 seasons, opponent-adjusted, weighted by dropbacks with a 1-season half-life, shrunk to the recruiting-class prior (247/On3 composite rating mapped to expected EPA/play from historical FBS QBs) with k = 150 dropbacks. Swap value = (starter - replacement) EPA/dropback x team dropbacks per game (about 35 to 45) x 0.75 points per EPA-equivalent play; report mean and posterior SD. As-of timestamp = last confirmed depth-chart or beat-report vintage before kickoff.
free_sources: CFBD plays and PPA endpoints (free key)

cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.label: Snap-weighted availability loss
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.mechanism: Aggregates all known absences (any position) into a single points-per-game value using snap share times player value over replacement.
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.rationale: College injury information is sparse, so the model needs a way to price a partial list (two starting linemen out, a corner doubtful) consistently; counting injuries is wrong because snap load and positional value differ by factors of five or more.
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.measurement: For each missing or doubtful player i: loss_i = P(out_i) x snap_share_i(prior season or current season to date) x (grade_i - grade_replacement_pos) x positional_points_per_grade, with positional weights fitted from historical snap-weighted ratings (QB >> OT/CB > WR/DL > RB/TE/S). Sum over players, subtract nothing for the opponent. P(out) = 1.0 for confirmed out, 0.5 for doubtful or questionable, 0.15 for unreported-but-flagged. Grades from PFF where available, otherwise PPA-on-field proxy. Timestamp each source report.
free_sources: CFBD player usage and season stats (free key)

cfb.rating_posterior_sd.label: Team-rating posterior standard deviation
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.mechanism: Per-team uncertainty about true strength given games played, connectivity and roster churn; sets the width of the margin distribution.
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.rationale: A rating gap of 7 with SDs of 2.0 and 2.0 gives a different win probability than the same gap with SDs of 5.0 and 5.0 early in the season; ignoring estimation error makes September favourites look too safe and moves cover probabilities at every rung.
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.measurement: Bayesian state-space rating per team: prior mean from last season rating x returning-production shrinkage, prior SD 6 points at week 0 falling toward 2.5 by week 10 per the observed rating update; implement as posterior variance = 1 / (1/prior_var + n_eff / game_sd^2) with game_sd = 13 points and n_eff = sum of connectivity-weighted game weights. Add portal-churn variance inflation proportional to 1 - returning production. Use margin-difference SD sqrt(sd_home^2 + sd_away^2 + 13^2 x (1 + 0.3 x pace_variance_term)).
free_sources: CFBD games and returning production (free key)

cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.label: Large-spread cover curve from non-market rating gap
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.mechanism: Empirical probability that the favourite's margin exceeds k, as a function of pre-game rating gap and opponent class (FBS vs FCS, G5 vs P4).
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.rationale: Rungs such as FAU by more than 41.5 sit in a regime where starters are removed, the clock runs and margin growth is truncated; a Gaussian around the rating gap overstates the tail, and the truncation point differs for FCS opponents and for coaches who keep scoring.
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.measurement: From historical FBS games (2014 onward), bin pre-game rating gap (non-market, SP+ or own rating) in 3-point buckets; for each bucket compute the empirical survival function P(margin >= k) for k in {1..60} with isotonic smoothing and a beta prior of strength 30 games on the pooled curve. Estimate separate curves for FCS opponents, neutral site, and for coaches in the top and bottom tercile of historical starter-pull time. Output is a vector of probabilities per rung, evaluated as-of kickoff.

cfb.fourth_down_aggression.label: Fourth-down aggression and clock-management index
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.mechanism: Coach tendency to go for it, onside, and to run or save clock, which changes margin variance and end-of-game scoring.
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.rationale: Aggressive coaches convert field goals into possible touchdowns or turnovers on downs, widening the margin distribution; conservative leaders reduce late scoring. Two teams of equal rating but different aggression produce different cover rates for a rung.
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.measurement: For each head coach, 4th-down go-for-it rate over expected from a fitted model (yard line, distance, score diff, time) = observed go rate - model go rate for the same situations, computed over last 2 seasons with k = 40 situations shrinkage; add mean seconds of clock burned per play when leading by 8-24 in Q4 versus the conference median. Coach change resets to a coach-career prior; compute as-of week.

cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.label: Conference schedule grid and correlated win-count simulation inputs
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.mechanism: For the count-of-teams-with-10+-wins contracts: the conference game grid (who plays whom, home/away, byes) plus non-conference opponents define each team win probability vector, and shared rating uncertainty plus intra-conference head-to-head games make team outcomes dependent.
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.rationale: The count is not a Poisson-binomial of independent teams: every intra-conference game gives one team a win and another a loss, so wins are negatively dependent within the conference, while a shared conference-strength error (cross-conference calibration) makes them positively dependent. The two forces change the variance of the count and therefore the tail rung (5+ Big 12, 7+ Big Ten, 8+ SEC). Regular season only, so championship games and bowls are excluded from the count.
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.measurement: For each conference, take the 2026 schedule as of the as-of date: for every game g compute P(home win) from a non-market rating difference (cfb.sp_plus or own rating) plus venue term, with each team rating drawn once per simulation from N(rating, cfb.rating_posterior_sd^2) and a conference-level shift drawn from N(0, tau_c^2) with tau_c estimated from the historical dispersion of cross-conference results (start tau_c=1.5 points, to be fitted). Simulate 20,000 seasons, count teams with >=10 regular-season wins (FCS opponents count as wins) and read P(count>=K). Re-run weekly using results to date as fixed; report the simulated count variance against the independent-Poisson-binomial variance as a diagnostic.
free_sources: CFBD games and schedule endpoints (free key)

cfb.season_max_total_tail.label: Season maximum-total tail model across all Division I games
cfb.season_max_total_tail.mechanism: KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE settles on the single largest combined score over every Division I regular-season game including overtime, so it is an extreme-value quantity of roughly 850 game totals, driven by FBS-vs-FCS mismatches, multi-overtime games and pace-and-defence-poor matchups.
cfb.season_max_total_tail.rationale: The rung 144.5 sits far in the tail; the maximum total is governed by rare pairings (two fast, weak defences, or a long overtime game where each overtime adds up to 8 points) rather than the mean total. A Gaussian game-total model badly understates it, so the tail needs an empirical or Poisson-compound fit with a separate overtime-length component.
cfb.season_max_total_tail.measurement: Collect the maximum regular-season Division I total per season 2005-2025 (FBS and FCS games, including overtime) and the full set of per-game totals above 100. Fit a generalised Pareto tail to game totals above 95 points with a threshold chosen by mean-excess plot; scale the exceedance rate by the number of games (about 850 FBS-involved and more with FCS-FCS games) and add a multi-overtime component: P(k overtimes) from cfb.ot_model, with 2-point-only possessions after the second overtime. Output P(max total > K) for K in 120..160 and the number of games expected above 100. As-of date uses only completed seasons plus current-season games already played.
free_sources: CFBD games (FBS and some FCS, free key)

cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.label: Script-adjusted team dropbacks
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.mechanism: Expected team pass attempts plus sacks given the expected game flow, rather than the season-average pass rate.
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.rationale: Pass volume is the largest driver of receiving-yards variance: a team that trails by two scores throws 50-plus times, a team leading by 21 throws 20. Using season-average attempts mixes games of both kinds and understates the spread in the mean.
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.measurement: Fit dropbacks per game on team neutral-situation pass rate (first and second down, score within 7, first three quarters), opponent neutral pass-rate allowed, expected margin from non-market ratings (not a quote), and plays; then predict at the pre-game expected margin with a piecewise term at +/-14 and +/-21. Window: current season with 6-game half-life, shrunk to previous season with k = 4 games; as-of the Saturday preceding kickoff. Output: mean attempts and a negative-binomial dispersion.
free_sources: CFBD plays with down, distance, score and play type (free key)

cfb.state_dependent_pace.label: State-dependent tempo (seconds per play by score state)
cfb.state_dependent_pace.mechanism: Plays per minute differ when leading, tied or trailing, and by clock situation; determines total plays inside 60 minutes plus any overtime.
cfb.state_dependent_pace.rationale: A hurry-up team trailing can add 8 to 12 plays versus its average; a ball-control team leading runs the clock. The season mean hides this, and the rule set since 2023 (clock running after first downs outside the last two minutes) changed the baseline.
cfb.state_dependent_pace.measurement: For each offence compute seconds per snap in four buckets (trailing by 9+, within 8, leading 9-16, leading 17+) in Q1-Q4, excluding two-minute drills, over the last 12 games with 0.5 shrink toward conference mean (k = 200 snaps). Combine with the opponent's pace allowed and expected state mix from the script input to produce expected snaps; flag the season's clock-rule regime. As-of last completed game.

cfb.completion_yardage_profile.label: Completion yardage profile (depth of target and yards after catch)
cfb.completion_yardage_profile.mechanism: Splits yards per completion into air yards and yards after catch and records the explosive-completion rate.
cfb.completion_yardage_profile.rationale: Two offences with the same yards per attempt can have very different variance: one dinks and runs screens, the other throws deep. Threshold probabilities depend on the tail of long completions and on the opponent's tackling and safety depth.
cfb.completion_yardage_profile.measurement: Per team: average depth of target, YAC per completion, share of completions of 20+ and 40+ yards, all opponent-adjusted by the opponent's allowed values; 10-game window with 0.7 per-game decay and shrinkage k = 60 completions to conference mean. Where air-yards data is missing (CFBD has limited coverage), approximate with yards per completion and 20+ rate. Report mean and SD of yards per completion.
free_sources: CFBD plays (yards, play text parse, free key)
PFF/SIS charting for air yards (paid, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for CFB depth)

cfb.wr_personnel_rate.label: Receiver personnel-grouping rate
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.mechanism: Share of snaps with 3 or more receivers (11 personnel, 10 personnel, empty sets) versus heavy sets.
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.rationale: Receiving-yards volume depends on how many pass-catchers are deployed: spread offences convert dropbacks into more targets to receivers and fewer to backs and tight ends, and the loss of a receiver matters more when the team lives in 4-wide sets.
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.measurement: For each offence, share of snaps by personnel group (RB/TE/WR counts) over the last 8 games, opponent-weighted; compute the 3+ WR snap share and empty-set rate with k = 150 snap shrinkage to conference average. Combine with receiver snap shares and starters out as of the pregame vintage.
free_sources: No free CFB personnel feed confirmed (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)

cfb.expected_possessions.label: Expected combined possessions per game
cfb.expected_possessions.mechanism: Number of drives in the game computed from both teams' seconds per drive rather than from averaged plays.
cfb.expected_possessions.rationale: Total points scale with the number of possessions, roughly 22-26 combined in modern FBS games. Seconds per play, plays per drive and run/pass mix interact: two slow teams produce fewer possessions than the average of their individual paces implies, because clock-killing drives are shared.
cfb.expected_possessions.measurement: For each team compute average drive duration (seconds) on non-garbage-time drives over last 10 games with 0.8 per-game decay, excluding drives ending a half; expected possessions per team = (3600 - stoppage-adjusted halftime-neutral time) / (0.5*(d_own + d_opp_allowed)) with a clock-regime constant fitted by season; add 1 when either team has no-huddle rate above 40 percent. Report mean and SD (about 2 possessions). As-of the last completed game.
free_sources: CFBD drives (start time, duration, plays; free key)

cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.label: Points per scoring opportunity (drives crossing opponent 40)
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.mechanism: Average points on drives that reach the opponent 40 or closer, opponent-adjusted, separating finishing from moving the ball.
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.rationale: A team can have strong PPA and still score few points if it settles for field goals; conversely, strong finishers outperform yardage. Scoring-trip efficiency regresses less than red-zone TD rate because it pools more drives and includes field-goal-range situations.
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.measurement: Per team: sum of points on drives with first down inside the opponent 40 divided by number of such drives (over 10 games, 0.85 per-game decay), adjusted by opponent allowed value and by kicker field-goal value; shrink with k = 25 drives toward conference mean. Output mean and SE; combine own offence and opposing defence by an additive deviation model.

cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.label: Defensive and special-teams touchdown rate
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.mechanism: Rate at which a team scores on interception returns, fumble returns, kickoff and punt returns, and blocked kicks, and allows them.
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.rationale: These touchdowns add 6-8 points without using an offensive possession, are partly skill (returners, ball-hawks) and mostly luck, and fatten the right tail of the total. The market's total rarely prices them separately.
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.measurement: For each team: defensive plus special-teams touchdowns scored and allowed per game over 2 seasons with 0.5 season decay, shrunk with k = 12 games toward the FBS mean per team-game (to be measured, plausibly 0.1 to 0.2); add a return-specialist indicator from kick returner yards over expected. Output expected points = 7 x rate (own) + 7 x rate allowed by opponent minus offence replaced.

cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.label: Stadium wind exposure and forecast bias
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.mechanism: Translates a forecast wind speed into expected on-field wind by stadium (open bowl, enclosed, dome, orientation).
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.rationale: A 20 mph forecast at a closed or dome stadium is irrelevant while the same forecast at an open lakeside stadium cuts passing and field-goal range materially; the forecast vintage alone is not predictive without the exposure factor.
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.measurement: Per stadium: roof type (open, retractable, dome), historical ratio of observed on-field wind (from nearest airport station via NOAA ISD or Meteostat) to forecast at issue 6 hours out, fitted by month over 8 seasons; exposure = ratio x forecast. Outputs adjusted wind in mph and an indicator of >15 mph. Apply only at kickoff plus 3 hours.

cfb.regulation_tie_curve.label: Regulation tie probability curve from non-market expected margin and total
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.mechanism: Empirical P(margin = 0 after four quarters) as a function of absolute expected margin and expected total points.
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.rationale: A tie is a point mass on a lumpy lattice: the probability is roughly the margin density at zero adjusted for the fact that football scores come in 3, 6, 7, 8 and so ties occur preferentially at combined patterns that are reachable by both sides. The curve is peaked at zero gap and decays quickly, and the expected total changes the margin SD.
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.measurement: From all FBS games since 2005 (about 15,000 games: roughly 750 per season over 21 seasons), fit logistic/GAM of tie indicator on |expected margin| (from SP+ or own rating, not market) and expected total with monotone smoothing; bucket |gap| in 2-point bins (0-2, 2-4, ... 14+) and expected total in 8-point bins; shrink bins to pooled curve with prior strength 200 games. Evaluate as-of kickoff. Output P(tie) with 95 percent interval; for FCS fit separately.
free_sources: CFBD games with period line scores (free key)

cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.label: End-of-regulation decision profile
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.mechanism: How often a coach settles for a tie (kneel, kick the tying field goal) versus plays for the win in the last two minutes.
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.rationale: Tied games are created or avoided in the final minutes: a trailing team that kicks a field goal to tie creates overtime, and a team with the ball tied with 40 seconds left may kneel. Coaches differ systematically, so two matchups with equal margin distributions can differ in tie incidence.
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.measurement: From plays with clock under 2:00 in Q4 and score diff in {-3..-1, -8..-1 requiring TD+2, 0}: for each head coach compute the rate of choosing kneel/tying FG versus aggressive play over expected from a fitted decision model, over 3 seasons with shrinkage k = 15 situations to the conference mean. Output coach-level tie-propensity z-score; coach change resets to prior of coordinators plus career data.
free_sources: CFBD plays with clock and play_type (free key)

cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.label: Overtime possession scoring rates (touchdown, field goal, none)
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.mechanism: Per-team probabilities of touchdown, field goal or no score from the 25-yard line, offence and defence, opponent-adjusted.
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.rationale: Overtime ends when one team outscores the other in a period; probability a period ends tied depends on the pair of scoring outcome distributions, and overtime offence differs from ordinary offence (short field, no clock, kicker at 42 yards).
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.measurement: Per team: P(TD), P(FG), P(none) on first-and-10 from the 25 with no clock pressure, estimated from non-OT drives starting inside the opponent 30 with shrinkage k = 20 drives plus actual OT possessions with weight 3; opponent-adjust by the same quantity for defences. Period tie probability = sum over outcomes of own x opponent matched scores (TD-TD with equal conversion, FG-FG, none-none). Compute as-of date.

cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.label: Two-point conversion success rate for the alternating-attempt overtimes
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.mechanism: Team probability of converting a two-point attempt from the 3-yard line, offence and defence, used from the third overtime.
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.rationale: From the third overtime onward periods are single two-point attempts; a period ends tied whenever both teams convert or both fail, so the per-period tie chance is p_a p_b + (1 - p_a)(1 - p_b), close to one half for any plausible p, which keeps the process nearly memoryless and makes 9+ periods a power of about one half.
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.measurement: Per team: successful two-point attempts divided by attempts, offence and defence, over 3 seasons with beta prior at league mean of roughly 0.47-0.50 (to be estimated) and prior strength 25 attempts; use goal-to-go 3-yard plays with 2 or fewer yards to go as proxy where attempts are few. Combine as p_a = (off_a + (1 - def_b)) / 2. As-of date.
free_sources: CFBD plays: two-point conversion play types (free key)

cfb.season_ot_exposure.label: Season overtime exposure (games remaining and current maximum)
cfb.season_ot_exposure.mechanism: Number of remaining Division I games in the regular season and the maximum overtime periods already seen.
cfb.season_ot_exposure.rationale: KXNCAAFMOSTOT is a season-extreme event: if a nine-overtime game has already occurred the market is decided, otherwise the number of remaining games times the per-game probability of reaching 9+ periods determines the price. The decay of exposure through the season is a deterministic input.
cfb.season_ot_exposure.measurement: Count remaining Division I regular-season games as of query date (FBS plus FCS, per the contract's scope) by week; current season maximum number of overtime periods across all D-I games; P(YES) = 1 - (1 - q)^N with q from the tie curve x period-length geometric (with regime change at OT 3), unless max already >= 9 (then 1.0). Update weekly.

cfb.period_possession_allocation.label: Period possession allocation (opening kick, deferral and end-of-half order)
cfb.period_possession_allocation.mechanism: Expected possessions per team in each quarter given who receives the opening kickoff, deferral habits and tempo.
cfb.period_possession_allocation.rationale: A quarter has only about 2-3 possessions per team, and receiving the opening kickoff gives one extra drive in Q1 (and typically ends Q2 with the other team holding the ball); the share swings expected quarter margin by 0.3 to 0.8 points between the two possession orders. The toss itself is only known at kickoff, so the input must be probabilistic.
cfb.period_possession_allocation.measurement: Per head coach: P(defer | win toss) over last 3 seasons (shrink k = 10 tosses to the conference mean) and P(win toss) = 0.5; P(team receives first) = 0.5 x P(receive | win) + 0.5 x (1 - opponent P(defer)). Expected drives per quarter per team = season drives per team x quarter share (0.24-0.26 each) with Q1 and Q3 adjusted by the receive-first indicator times 0.5 drive. Store the realised toss only after kickoff.
free_sources: CFBD games and plays (kickoff and coin toss from play text, free key)

cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.label: Two-minute and end-of-half drive efficiency
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.mechanism: Points per drive in the final two minutes of the first half and of the game, plus the share of drives where the leader runs out the clock.
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.rationale: Quarters 2 and 4 end with clock-driven scoring chances that are not representative of normal drives; a good two-minute offence with a reliable kicker produces points at a much higher rate, and teams differ in whether they play to score or hold the ball at the end of the half.
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.measurement: For each team: points per drive in the last 2:00 of Q2 and Q4 when score within 14 and at least one timeout, over 2 seasons, with 0.5 decay per season and shrinkage k = 20 drives to the conference mean; include kneel-down rate (drives ending in kneels when leading) and no-timeout slot. Compute opponent-adjusted by the opponent's allowed value.
free_sources: CFBD plays and drives with clock (free key)

cfb.period_margin_lattice.label: Period margin lattice and tie mass by expected margin and total
cfb.period_margin_lattice.mechanism: Empirical probabilities of period margin = 0, positive margins up to 8+, by period and by pre-game expected margin and total.
cfb.period_margin_lattice.rationale: In a single quarter the most likely outcome for evenly matched teams is a tie (0-0 or equal scores) and the winner market loses on ties; spread rungs at 7.5 correspond to a touchdown-plus-two margin or more, so they live in the thin right tail of a lumpy distribution. A Gaussian misprices both the mass at zero and the key numbers.
cfb.period_margin_lattice.measurement: From FBS games since 2014 take the line scores by period; for each period and for each of expected-margin bins (-14 to +14 in 3-point bins, from non-market ratings) and expected-total bins (3 bins) estimate P(margin = k) for k in {-14..14} with Dirichlet smoothing (prior strength 100 games, centred on a compound-Poisson model). Evaluate as of kickoff and output joint probabilities of tie, win and cover at each rung.

cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.label: Second-half overtime spillover
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.mechanism: Expected effect of overtime on the second-half margin, which includes overtime points by contract.
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.rationale: For second-half sides, overtime points are added to each team's second-half total; a game that is tied after regulation is decided by overtime, so the second-half margin equals the overtime result plus second-half regulation margin; ignoring this biases second-half winner probabilities for the close games where it matters.
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.measurement: P(OT) from a tie curve (bucketed by non-market expected margin and total) x distribution of OT margin (home/away first possession, points scored by period one: roughly 7 versus 3 versus 0); output expected spillover to the second-half margin = P(OT) x E[OT margin | team] and a variance increment. For 4Q and Q1-Q3 contracts set to zero because they exclude overtime.

cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.label: Joint four-quarter scoring pmf with per-team scoreless mass and highest-quarter argmax
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.mechanism: Distribution of each quarter combined points and each team points jointly across Q1-Q4, with quarter-to-quarter correlation, used to price both-teams-to-score in a quarter and the highest-scoring-quarter contract with its 1/N tie split.
